approaches.title: Parity-based greedy accumulation
approaches.summary: Sums values at even and odd indices separately and returns the larger total. This greedy strategy is incorrect because the optimal robbery pattern need not follow a fixed parity.

revisions.shortChangeSummary: Attempts to solve the problem greedily by comparing the sums of houses at even and odd indices. This approach is marked wrong because it can miss the optimal non-adjacent selection.

approaches.title: Dynamic programming with rolling state
approaches.summary: Uses the recurrence that the best result at each house is the maximum of skipping it or adding its value to the result from two houses earlier. The implementation evolves from a full one-dimensional table to constant-space state and then a fold expression.

revisions.shortChangeSummary: Replaces the incorrect greedy strategy with one-dimensional dynamic programming, storing the best result through each index.
Preserves the dynamic programming recurrence while reducing storage to two rolling state values.
Refactors the rolling dynamic program into an iterator fold without changing the underlying strategy.
